newsitem.title: CANADA: Manitoba has C$90.8 mln surplus in fiscal 1996-97.
newsitem.headline: Manitoba has C$90.8 mln surplus in fiscal 1996-97.

text.p: The Western Canadian province of Manitoba on Thursday estimated a budget surplus of C$90.8 million in fiscal 1996-97 ended March 31.
Manitoba forecast a C$27 million surplus for fiscal 1997-98, it's third consecutive surplus. The 1996-97 surplus exceeded the previous projection of a C$55.7 million surplus.

"Despite the considerable expenditure pressures during 1996-97, particularly the C$68 million more than budgeted in health, the continued strong performance of Manitoba's economy resulted in revenues exceeding our initial projections," Manitoba Finance Minister Eric Stefanson said in a statement.
Individual and corporate income tax receipts increased by C$34.6 million and led the fourth-quarter revision.
The balance was attributed to fourth-quarter increases in various revenue sources such as retail sales tax, corporation capital tax and vehicle registration fees.
Net proceeds from the sale of Manitoba Telecom Services Inc totaled C$414.6 million, with the government using C$150 million to pay down health sector debt.

The rest of the proceeds from the MTS divestiture, which totaled C$264.6 million, along with the C$90.8 million budget surplus, will be put in Manitoba's fiscal stabilization fund. That fund totaled C$577.1 million at March 31, 1997.
